A general category of techniques sampling volume data along rays.
Ray Evaluation Stepping DVR is a specific implementation within this category using fixed steps and modular shader defines. [Link](1735-ray-marching-volume-rendering.md)
Focuses specifically on marching through density fields.
Ray Evaluation Stepping DVR extends this by including color, BRDF, and transfer function evaluation. [Link](3462-density-marching.md)
An alternative approach that pre-integrates volume data into a discrete integral.
Ray Evaluation Stepping DVR performs integration on-the-fly during ray marching. [Link](3552-discrete-volume-rendering-integral-vri.md)
A specialized technique for light shafts.
Ray Evaluation Stepping DVR is a general-purpose DVR method, not specific to light shafts. [Link](3873-volumetric-light-shafts-urp-raymarching.md)
*   **Time Complexity**: $O(N)$ where $N$ is the number of steps along the ray, determined by $stepsize$ and ray length.
*   **Memory Complexity**: $O(1)$ per thread for the marching state, plus $O(V)$ for the volume data storage.
Early-out can significantly reduce average step count.
Supports both world-space and object-space indexing.
Requires careful configuration of density ranges.
*   **When to use**: When flexible transfer function and blending integration is needed, and the volume supports the required indexing mode.
*   **When not to use**: When adaptive step size is required for high-frequency details, or when the volume does not support the required indexing mode and adaptive stepping is critical.
